articles.title: Djokovic derrota a Borges y sigue invicto en China después de 11 años
articles.standfirst: El serbio se clasifica para octavos del China Open, donde su balance es de 30-0
articles.summary: El serbio se clasifica para octavos del China Open, donde su balance es de 30-0
articles.body: El serbio Novak Djokovic (n.11) derrotó este miércoles al portugués Nuno Borges (n.49) por 6-3 y 7-6(2) y avanzó a los octavos de final del Abierto de China, donde elevó a treinta victorias sin derrotas su balance en su regreso al torneo once años después. El encuentro duró una hora y 52 minutos sobre la pista dura de la central Diamond del Centro Nacional de Tenis de Pekín, abarrotada para recibir al seis veces campeón del certamen. La espera terminó con un triunfo que exigió al serbio superar dos oportunidades de rotura en la primera manga, recibir atención del fisioterapeuta en la segunda y resolver un desempate ante un Borges que mantuvo la resistencia hasta el tramo final. Djokovic comenzó apoyado en un primer servicio que le permitía tomar la iniciativa tras el resto del portugués. Rompió en el segundo juego y confirmó la ventaja para situarse 3-0, mientras Borges buscaba desplazarlo por el fondo y obligarlo a golpear en movimiento. El momento más delicado del primer set llegó en el séptimo juego, cuando dos dobles faltas consecutivas abrieron una puerta al portugués. Con las gradas volcadas en su apoyo, el serbio salvó dos bolas de rotura y sacó adelante un turno de casi diez minutos. También dejó una de las imágenes del encuentro al mover a Borges desde el fondo antes de subir a la red y recordar que la volea no se pelotea, con un golpe definitivo que levantó al público y le dio ventaja en aquel juego. Borges abrió la segunda manga con un juego en blanco, pero Djokovic respondió con un saque directo y una combinación de dejada y globo que volvió a encender las gradas. Tras el quinto juego, el serbio solicitó atención del fisioterapeuta por unas molestias que no le impidieron continuar. Al regresar, conservó su servicio en blanco para igualar 3-3. El portugués tampoco cedió. Su mayor prueba llegó en el noveno juego, que se prolongó durante casi quince minutos y en el que salvó una bola de rotura. Djokovic ganó un intercambio de 28 golpes, pero Borges encontró apoyo en su saque para mantener la igualdad. Sin quiebres en la manga, el desenlace quedó para el desempate. Allí, el serbio abrió una ventaja de 5-1 y cerró por 7-2, acompañado por las celebraciones de una grada que podrá volver a verlo en octavos. Djokovic terminó con ocho saques directos y ganó el 88 % de los puntos disputados con su primer servicio. Su próxima rivalidad será con el chino Bu Yunchaokete (n.104), vencedor del argentino Juan Manuel Cerúndolo (n.53).

images.caption: Novak Djokovic tras derrotar a Nuno Borges en China. Lapresse

articles.title: China Open: Novak Djokovic wins first match since Wimbledon
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic beats Nuno Borges at the China Open to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic maintained his remarkable unbeaten record at the China Open as he beat Nuno Borges to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July.

The 39-year-old former world number one struggled in the second set but came through to win 6-3 7-6 (7-2) for his 30th consecutive victory in Beijing, albeit in his first appearance at the event since 2015.

Djokovic revealed in August that he has been dealing with an underlying health condition that causes particular issues in hot, humid conditions for "the past couple of years" and was far from his best against Portuguese Borges.

During the second set he used his racquet to help stretch his back between games and needed a medical timeout to receive treatment to his right shoulder.

But despite that Djokovic battled to victory in one hour and 50 minutes to set up a second-round match against wildcard Bu Yunchaokete of China.

Playing in the tournament for the first time in 11 years, the Serb, a 24-time Grand Slam champion, is bidding to win the China Open for a record-extending seventh time.

Meanwhile, Great Britain's Katie Boulter is through to the second round in the women's draw with a straight-set victory over Mai Hontama of Japan.

Boulter, 30, claimed a 6-3 6-4 win and will now face Czech seventh seed Karolina Muchova in the next round.

images.caption: Image caption, Novak Djokovic has won six titles at the China Open between 2009 and 2015

articles.title: Nagami y la Rafa Nadal Academy unen deporte, diseño e innovación en el 10º aniversario de la Academia
articles.standfirst: La empresa española de Arquitectura y Diseño, reconocida internacionalmente por su liderazgo en la impresión 3D, se suma al emotivo regreso de Rafa Nadal a las pistas
articles.summary: La empresa española de Arquitectura y Diseño, reconocida internacionalmente por su liderazgo en la impresión 3D, se suma al emotivo regreso de Rafa Nadal a las pistas
articles.body: Con motivo del 10º aniversario de la Rafa Nadal Academy, Nagami, empresa española de Arquitectura y Diseño reconocida internacionalmente por su liderazgo en la impresión 3D a gran escala, se une a una celebración especialmente significativa: la primera vez que Rafa Nadal cogerá una raqueta en público desde su retirada del tenis profesional. Para acompañar este momento único, la Academia ha querido confiar en Nagami para crear una pieza especialmente concebida para la ocasión, poniendo en valor la conexión entre excelencia deportiva, innovación y compromiso con el medio ambiente. Nagami desarrolla proyectos y piezas de diseño mediante tecnología de impresión 3D robótica de gran escala utilizando plásticos reciclados. Esta apuesta por la economía circular y la protección de nuestros ecosistemas constituye uno de los puntos de conexión entre Nagami y Rafa Nadal Academy, ambos comprometidos con la necesidad de proteger nuestro entorno y generar un impacto positivo a través de sus respectivos ámbitos. Bajo su filosofía “From Waste to Beauty”, Nagami transforma residuos en piezas de diseño que combinan creatividad, innovación tecnológica y responsabilidad medioambiental. El diseño del trofeo creado especialmente para el 10º aniversario de la Rafa Nadal Academy nace de la unión de dos iconos: el tenis y el característico toro que identifica a Rafa Nadal. Su forma describe una transición desde una base octogonal, que recuerda al puño de una raqueta, hasta el “bull”, el logo de Rafa Nadal, en la parte superior. La pieza interpreta estos elementos desde una perspectiva contemporánea, trasladando la fuerza, precisión y excelencia asociadas al deporte de élite al lenguaje del diseño y la fabricación digital. El resultado es una pieza que representa la unión entre excelencia deportiva, economía circular e innovación industrial española, convirtiendo un material que en otro contexto sería considerado residuo en un objeto de valor, significado y belleza.

articles.title: Emma Navarro: US star opens up on health struggles
articles.summary: American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" as she shares her long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.
articles.body:
American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" after opening up on long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.

Navarro, who claimed her first title in more than a year at the Strasbourg Open in May, is currently ranked 24th in the world.

The 25-year-old was as high as eighth in 2024, the year she reached the quarter-finals at the Australian Open and Wimbledon, and the last four at the US Open in her native New York.

But towards the end of 2025 she was diagnosed with relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) and subsequently found out she was suffering with the autoimmune disorder Hashimoto's hypothyroidism.

Those issues contributed to her losing nine of her first 13 matches in 2026 and withdrawing from the Charleston Open at the end of March.

She says she initially ignored problems that dogged her for three years due to exceeding her expectations on the court.

"Being new to professional tennis, I was doing what my team and I thought was best, and pushing myself to the limit was always my MO," she wrote in a lengthy post on Instagram. , external

"And it worked. From the outside, things looked great. I continued to achieve tennis milestones that far exceeded my expectations, my ranking was rising, my level continued to improve, I continued to get faster and more athletic on the court, and I looked to be the strongest, fittest version of myself I had ever been."

Yet the warning signs were there. She lost about 14kg in weight during 2023 and 2024, and her breakthrough WTA Tour victory at the Hobart International, Australia proved a bittersweet moment.

"I was off. I was experiencing emotions I had never experienced before, at least not to this severity. Irritability, frustration, perfectionism, worry, and bizarrely for me, anger," she added.

"I remember feeling deep internal anger on the court that week in Hobart, like I wanted to smash every racket in my bag (something I had never done or wanted to do).

"Everything began to annoy me. My team, other people, anything that didn't align with my specific preferences or routines, any imperfection on the court, every mistake, every point I lost. But I tried my hardest to not let people see how I felt, to keep it together. Additionally, I was hungry. Every hour of the day, I was hungry."

Navarro, went on to explain how she had struggled with "headaches, dizziness, brain fog, fatigue, anxiousness and mood swings" through 2025, before meeting with doctors and nutritionists and various specialists, and realising she had been under-fueling for almost the entire period.

While she is missing the Asian swing as part of her recovery for next season, she added: "I gained some weight this year. But I also gained my life back. I have enough energy to seize every day, to train or compete as hard as I want to, and to live a life outside of tennis."

articles.title: Patrick McEnroe on U.S. Open weed smell, trans athletes, foreign recruits reshaping college tennis
articles.summary: Patrick McEnroe is taking his fight over foreign recruits in college tennis to Capitol Hill, backing a new bill heading before the House now.
articles.body: Tennis icon Patrick McEnroe is pushing for federal reform in college athletics while weighing in on transgender participation and the mysterious weed stench that hit the U.S. Open this year. Appearing on OutKick's "Tomi Lahren is Fearless," the former U.S. Davis Cup captain sounded the alarm on foreign recruits dominating American college rosters, calling tennis the ultimate "canary in the coal mine." Watching a marquee matchup between top SEC and ACC teams, McEnroe noticed a staggering imbalance: 21 of the 24 players on court were foreign recruits. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! McEnroe stressed, "So I knew that the numbers were getting pretty high in tennis. I've been in tennis my whole life. I played college tennis, had an amazing experience, and I became, quite frankly, deeply concerned." McEnroe is taking a stand in order to award the most opportunities possible to American collegiate athletes. The response prompted McEnroe to pen a Wall Street Journal op-ed and take his fight straight to Capitol Hill, meeting with Washington politicians to push a new bill currently heading before the House of Representatives. SENATE MOVES TO REIN IN COLLEGE SPORTS 'WILD WEST' WITH SWEEPING NEW RULES FOR PLAYERS, SCHOOLS "American universities were put in place, the athletic departments, to help our kids, to educate them, to give them opportunity," McEnroe argued, stressing U.S. schools should prioritize domestic talent over international pros. McEnroe didn't pull punches on trans athletes in women's sports either. As a father of three daughters, McEnroe wants to protect young girls in sports. "I'm not for a trans playing in female sports, no, I'm not," McEnroe said. The veteran broadcaster also weighed in on the marijuana haze that disrupted play at the U.S. Open, urging complaining players to lighten up. McEnroe blamed tournament workers taking quick breaks on the street behind the venue. TENNIS STAR ARYNA SABALENKA SUPPORTS WTA TRANSGENDER RULES, SAYS MALES SHOULDN'T FACE WOMEN "Instead of taking a break and having some Gatorade, I guess they were taking a little puff," he joked. Broadcasting one night with brother John, Patrick admitted he actually misses the old days when charcoal grill smoke drifted over the courts. COCO GAUFF APPEARS TO SUPPORT WTA EFFORTS TO PROTECT SPORT'S FAIRNESS, LAMENTS 'ATTACK' ON TRANS COMMUNITY "I kind of miss the smell of the burger," McEnroe laughed. "A little weed, if I smelled it in the air, wouldn't affect me as much as a burger, the smell from the charcoal of the burger." "Get over it," McEnroe declared. "Making a mountain out of a molehill, not that big of a deal." articles.title: China Open: Sonay Kartal wins on return, Arthur Fery beaten in Tokyo
articles.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal wins on her return to the WTA Tour after six months out with injury as she beats Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open.
articles.body:
Britain's Sonay Kartal won on her return to the WTA Tour after almost six months out with injury as she beat Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open.

The 24-year-old injured her lower back at Indian Wells in March and only made her return to tennis at the Billie Jean King Cup on 22 September.

Kartal, who narrowly lost to Czech world number 26 Marie Bouzkova on that return last week, produced a confident performance in Beijing to beat Spain's Lazaro Garcia 6-2 6-3.

The Briton broke the qualifier's serve five times - helped by four double faults from her opponent - and landed 69% of her first serves.

World number 129 Kartal will face Chinese 31st seed Wang Xinyu next as she bids to work her way back up the world rankings.

Fellow Briton Cameron Norrie lost 7-6 (7-1) 6-4 to US Open champion and world number two Alexander Zverev, while Harriet Dart is in action later on Thursday.

Elsewhere, British number one Arthur Fery fell 6-4 3-6 6-4 to Portuguese lucky loser Jaime Faria in the Japan Open first round.

Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz claimed a rusty 7-6 (7-1) 4-6 6-1 win over Alex Michelsen as he made his return to the ATP Tour.

Spanish world number three Alcaraz was sidelined for just over five months with a wrist injury before returning at the US Open, where he reached the quarter-finals.

Alcaraz struggled on serve against Michelsen, committing five double faults to five aces.

However, he saved five of the 13 break points he faced to advance and set up a second-round meeting with Italy's Matteo Arnaldi.

Denmark's Holger Rune also lost on his first ATP Tour appearance for almost a year.

Former world number four Rune tore his Achilles tendon in October 2025 and has since dropped out of the top 100.

He was beaten 6-3 6-1 by France's Kyrian Jacquet in Tokyo.

images.caption: Image caption, Sonay Kartal beat two seeded players before injuring her back at Indian Wells in March

articles.title: Munar dinamita el torneo de Tokio y acerca a Jódar al 'top10' mundial
articles.standfirst: El mallorquín supera a Fritz, finalista de la pasada edición, en la primera ronda
articles.summary: El mallorquín supera a Fritz, finalista de la pasada edición, en la primera ronda
articles.body: Jaume Munar, el 64 del ranking ATP y que se ganó el billete para el cuadro del Open 500 de Tokio desde la fase previa, ha dado la primera gran sorpresa del certamen este jueves al eliminar a Taylor Fritz, tercer favorito, por 6-7(7), 6-4 y 6-3, en 2 horas y 58 minutos. Es el quinto triunfo de Munar ante un 'top10' a lo largo de su carrera en un total de 28 partidos. El mallorquín circula por la parte alta del cuadro, la misma de su compatriota Carlos Alcaraz, con el que podría medirse en unas hipotéticas semifinales. A Jaume le espera en la siguiente ronda el portugués Jaime Faria, 'lucky loser' de la fase previa. Munar llega al final del curso en un buen estado de forma. Ya son tres las victorias que acumula en suelo japonés. Fritz, su víctima, pagó su paso por la Laver Cup de Londres y no podrá defender la final de la última edición en Tokio. El estadounidense tuvo el sábado dos pelotas de partido ante Alcaraz en el 02 Arena de Londres. Taylor no ha sido la única víctima de la Laver Cup. En esa lista de víctimas también están Flavio Cobolli, Casper Ruud, Brandon Nakashima, Ignacio Buse y Arthur Fery, eliminados a la primera en el inicio de la gira asiática. Eso le supone perder 330 puntos y cae al decimosegundo puesto del ranking. Rafa Jódar está un poco más cerca de ser 'top10'. El madrileño se encuentra a 491 puntos de la décima posición, que ocupa hoy el australiano Álex de Miñaur.

articles.title: Paula Badosa pierde ocho veces el saque... y pasa a la segunda ronda del WTA 1000 de Pekín
articles.standfirst: La catalana remonta un set a Kasatkina en un partido marcado por los 16 'breaks'
articles.summary: La catalana remonta un set a Kasatkina en un partido marcado por los 16 'breaks'
articles.body: Paula Badosa, la 59 del ranking a sus 28 años, se ha clasificado este jueves para la segunda ronda del WTA 1000 de Pekín, un torneo que le traía malos recuerdos porque fue precisamente allí donde hace un año tuvo que dar por terminada la temporada tras retirarse por lesión en la tercera ronda que le enfrentaba a Karolina Muchova. Badosa ha sido capaz de remontar un set ante Daria Kasatkina a pesar de haber cedido su servicio en ocho ocasiones. Es cierto que su rival encajó también ocho 'breaks'. La pupila de Pol Toledo cerró un marcador favorable de 4-6, 7-6(7) y 6-4, en 2 horas y 38 minutos. Los restos se impusieron a los saques y Paula es mejor que su rival desde el fondo de la pista porque cuenta con un mayor arsenal de golpes. La española también fue capaz de darle la vuelta a un 2-5 en contra en la muerte súbita del segundo set y un 2-4 en la manga de desempate. Kasatkina tiene un agujero en el saque y su verdugo lo sabía y nunca se rindió. En la siguiente ronda, a Badosa le espera ya una cabeza de serie, que en este caso es la letona Jelena Ostapenko (24). De momento, celebra que ya le tiene ganado el cara a cara a Dasha: 5-4.

images.caption: Kasatkina intenta llegar a una pelota. ANDRES MARTINEZ CASARES

articles.title: China Open and Japan Open: Carlos Alcaraz, Harriet Dart, Sonay Kartal victorious, but Brits Cam Norrie, Arthur Fery knocked out
articles.summary: Asian swing of tennis season sees Carlos Alcaraz win in Tokyo, Brit Arthur Fery suffers defeat; In Beijing, Britain's Cam Norrie knocked out but Harriet Dart, Sonay Kartal win; watch ATP Japan Open and WTA/ATP China Open this week live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Alcaraz saved three set points before clinching a see-sawing opening set against American Alex Michelsen with a ​strong display in the tiebreak but continued to experiment with his new sped-up service motion and was broken twice early in the next set.

The ​23-year-old Spaniard, who had shown glimpses of his best form en ‌route to the US Open quarter-finals last month after his long injury layoff, recovered to move ahead but a ​double fault in the seventh game handed Michelsen a route back.

Michelsen capitalised and kept his composure in a tense finish to the second set where a fortunate netcord winner ​left Alcaraz stranded at the baseline and helped the 22-year-old American force ⁠a decider.

Alcaraz, who led Team Europe to a ⁠Laver Cup triumph over Team World on indoor courts in London last weekend, said the relentless rain in Tokyo limited his practice.

"It ‌was a different feeling. The ball comes bigger. The court performs a little bit slower than the indoor courts for sure, so it was freaky to adjust to that," Alcaraz ‌said.

"It was a little bit frustrating, not being able to play my game, my style, and play aggressive ... it was difficult but I'm really happy to accept and understand how I had to play and to get the win at the end.

"It was really important to have ⁠this feeling for the next round, to know what I have ​to do for the next matches."

A couple of breathtaking points gave ​Alcaraz a 2-0 lead in the final set and the seven-times Grand Slam ​champion used the launch pad to close out a comfortable victory on a day ⁠of big upsets in the ATP 500 tournament.

The top seed's win came after third seed Taylor Fritz fell to qualifier Jaume Munar 6-7 (7-9) 6-4 6-3, sixth seed Casper Ruud lost to Luciano ⁠Darderi 7-6 (7-3) 6-3 and seventh seed Tommy Paul suffered ​a 6-1 6-2 defeat by Alejandro Tabilo.

Holger Rune , the former world No 4 ​who is stepping up his comeback from an Achilles injury, also crashed out in a 6-3 6-1 loss to Kyrian Jacquet.

Exits for Norrie and Fery as Dart, Kartal progress

Norrie was beaten 7-6 (7-1) 6-4 by newly-crowned US Open champion Alexander Zverev in the first round of the China Open in Beijing.

The Briton blew a set point opportunity then collapsed in the subsequent tie-break after taking the first point.

Zverev, who is intent on closing in on world No 1 Jannik Sinner, who is not playing in China, grabbed the crucial break in the ninth game of the second set before sealing his victory.

It was Zverev's ninth consecutive main tour victory over Norrie, who was playing his first match since his disappointing early exit at Flushing Meadows.

British No 1 Fery was bundled out of the Japan Open in the first round with a shock 4-6 6-3 4-6 loss to Portugal's Jaime Faria.

Fery was originally scheduled to open the tournament against Italy's Lorenzo Musetti, but the world No 25 was a late withdrawal from the tournament due to a finger injury.

He was replaced by world No 68 Faria, who took a surprise early lead in Tokyo before Fery was able to settle and force a deciding third set.

However he was unable to break Faria's serve in the final set as the Portuguese wrapped up the win in just over two hours.

At the women's China Open, Kartal picked up her first victory on tour since March with a straight sets 6-2 6-3 victory over Spain's Andrea Lazaro Garcia , progressing to the second round.

Fellow Brit Dart also made it through to the second round, but had to come through a three-hour epic up against China's Qu Yihan in Beijing.

The 30-year-old Londoner eventually progressed via a 6-2 6-7 (5-7) 7-5 success.

Japan's Nishikori bids farewell to pro career

Kei Nishikori had an emotional farewell to his professional career in Tokyo as he lost 6-4 6-4 to second-seeded Frances Tiafoe .

The 36-year-old Nishikori, a former US Open finalist with a career-high ranking of No. 4, said earlier in the week that he had mixed feelings about in his last elite-level tournament on home soil.

"I am excited to play in Japan but I also know this is my last moment," he said. "So, it's kind of sad."

Nishikori announced in May that he planned to retire at the end of the year and was granted a wild card entry to the Japan Open, which he won in 2012 and 2014.

Nishikori missed the Australian Open in January with right shoulder pain and has been affected by injuries the last several years. He also missed last year's US Open.

Making his professional debut in 2007, Nishikori became the first Japanese player to advance to the final of a Grand Slam men's singles tournament when he reached the championship decider at the 2014 US Open in New York, which he lost in straight sets to Marin Cilic.

articles.title: Japan Open: Kei Nishikori retires from tennis after defeat by Frances Tiafoe in Tokyo
articles.summary: A tearful Kei Nishikori says he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ends his professional career at the Japan Open.
articles.body:
A tearful Kei Nishikori said he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ended his professional career at the Japan Open.

Nishikori, known as one of the best players to never win a Grand Slam, lost 6-4 6-4 to world number eight Frances Tiafoe in Tokyo.

The 36-year-old became the first Japanese man to reach a major final when he faced Marin Cilic in the 2014 US Open showpiece.

Nishikori beat then world number one Novak Djokovic on his way to the New York final and defeated Rafael Nadal for Olympic bronze at the 2016 Games in Rio.

He was, however, hampered by injuries throughout his 19-year career.

"Playing in Japan is always a special moment," an emotional Nishikori told his home crowd.

"I wish I could have put in a slightly more convincing performance. But I'm happy I kept fighting right to the end.

"I'm proud that I didn't give up and played right to the finish."

Djokovic wins first match since Wimbledon at China Open

GB's Kartal wins on WTA return after six months out

Navarro opens up on health struggles that caused 'deep anger' on court

After losing to Tiafoe, Nishikori did a lap of honour of the main showcourt in Tokyo - the place where he won the title in 2012 and 2014.

A video featuring Djokovic, three-time Grand Slam champion Andy Murray and 1989 French Open winner Michael Chang, congratulating Nishikori, was also played.

"Your resilience and fighting spirit, to always come back after a lot of adversity, is really commendable and admirable," Djokovic said.

"We had some great battles all over the world. I'm really glad you're ending your career in your town, your country, in front of your people.

"You're going to get the farewell you absolutely deserve."

Nishikori started playing aged five and moved to Florida as a 14-year-old to train.

He won 12 ATP Tour singles titles in his career and claimed 40 victories over top-10 players.

He was the first Japanese man to reach the top 10 of the world rankings and inspired numerous players, including four-time major champion Naomi Osaka.

His 72.5% win-rate in deciding sets is the third best in ATP Tour history, behind only Bjorn Borg (73.4%) and John McEnroe (72.8%).

images.caption: Image caption, Kei Nishikori beat Stan Wawrinka and Novak Djokovic on his way to the 2014 US Open final

articles.title: Zverev salva el debut de Pekín y va directo hacia el número 1 ATP
articles.standfirst: El alemán derrota al británico Norrie en dos sets y se sitúa a 1.330 puntos de Sinner
articles.summary: El alemán derrota al británico Norrie en dos sets y se sitúa a 1.330 puntos de Sinner
articles.body: No será su paso por la Laver Cup lo que frene a Alexander Zverev en sus aspiraciones de convertirse en el trigésimo nuevo número 1 del circuito masculino en detrimento de Jannik Sinner. Cuatro días después de jugar en el 02 Arena de Londres y dar a Europa el sexto título del torneo por equipos organizado por Roger Federer, el tenista de Hamburgo ha demostrado este jueves su condición de primer favorito en el Open 500 de Pekín. Ya son 57 partidos ganados por Sascha en el presente curso, más que nadie. El balance del alemán contra zurdos asusta: 47-1 desde Roland Garros 2023. "Estoy contento con mis cifras, pero hay que seguir, es lo único que importa", advierte. Zverev ha superado en el debut a Cameron Norrie, por 7-6(1) y 6-4, y se sitúa a 1.330 puntos del cetro ATP que sigue manteniendo el lesionado Sinner. El italiano, que no juega desde la consecución de su segundo título consecutivo en la hierba de Wimbledon, debe decidir si su rodilla está en condiciones de afrontar el Masters 1000 de Shanghái (7 al 18), la siguiente parada en el calendario tenístico. Jannik se borró la semana pasada de Pekín por lo que perdió los 500 puntos como campeón de 2025.

articles.title: Emma Navarro habla del síndrome que sufre: "He ganado peso... pero he recuperado las ganas de vivir"
articles.standfirst: La tenista se sincera sobre los problemas físicos y psicológicos que ha sufrido a raíz del Déficit Energético Relativo en el Deporte, que le diagnosticaron a finales de 2025
articles.summary: La tenista se sincera sobre los problemas físicos y psicológicos que ha sufrido a raíz del Déficit Energético Relativo en el Deporte, que le diagnosticaron a finales de 2025
articles.body: La tenista estadounidense Emma Navarro, exnúmero 8 del ranking WTA, se sinceró en redes sociales con una emotiva carta en la que resume los problemas físicos y psicológicos que ha sufrido en los tres últimos años debido al Síndrome de Deficiencia Energética Relativa en el Deporte (RED-S) que le fue diagnosticado a finales de 2025. Le tenista, que ha decidido parar con el objetivo de recuperarse al 100% de cara a la próxima temporada, explicó que este síndrome hace que "el cuerpo no reciba suficiente energía para responder a las exigencias de la actividad física y de la vida cotidiana". Navarro relató episodios de irritabilidad, frustración, ansiedad e ira inusuales para ella: "Algo no iba bien. Sentía emociones que nunca antes había experimentado, al menos no en tal medida". También apuntó que perdió cerca de 9 kilos durante 2023 al considerar que adelgazar podía mejorar su rendimiento. Pero no mejoraba. "Ya no era capaz de pensar ni de recordar las cosas. Mi cerebro funcionaba a ralentí y estaba cansado, al igual que mi cuerpo. Me despertaba tan cansada como cuando me iba a acostar", aseguró. Pese a todo, se convirtió en la número 8 del mundo tras su semifinal en el US Open de 2024. Después de varias consultas con especialistas, el diagnóstico llegó en noviembre de 2025. "Llevaba casi tres años sin energía. Mi cuerpo luchaba de todas las formas posibles. Llevaba años gritándome y yo lo ignoraba". Empezó a mejorar hace unos meses, gracias al cambio en la alimentación y al control de la glucemia. "He ganado peso este año, es cierto. Pero también he recuperado las ganas de vivir", admitió. Ahora, descansará para regresar con vistas al Open de Australia de 2027.

articles.title: Alcaraz empieza con remontada la defensa de la corona en Tokio y juega a ser Sampras
articles.standfirst: El estadounidense fue el último tenista capaz de repetir título un año después
articles.summary: El estadounidense fue el último tenista capaz de repetir título un año después
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha iniciado con éxito la defensa de la corona del Open de Tokio. El murciano, que busca defender cetro por sexta vez en su carrera (lo hizo antes en Barcelona, Mutua Madrid Open, Indian Wells, Wimbledon y Roland Garros), se deshizo este jueves del americano Alex Michelsen, por 7-6(1), 4-6 y 6-1, en 2 horas y 31 minutos. Carlitos aspira a ser el primer jugador que retiene el título en la capital japonesa desde Pete Sampras, campeón en 1993-94. Al pupilo de Samuel López le sientan bien los torneos de categoría 500. Y es que encadena 17 triunfos desde que perdió la final del Godó 2025 con Holger Rune. "No había podido entrenar al aire libre (por la lluvia) hasta el calentamiento de esta mañana, así que fue bastante distinto”, señaló el vencedor a la conclusión. “Las sensaciones son diferentes. Creo que la pelota viene con más peso. La pista es un poco más lenta que la cubierta, así que tuve que ajustar mi juego”. Michelsen, que venía de alcanzar los cuartos del US Open (dominaba dos sets a cero ante Frances Tiafoe), le puso las cosas difíciles al fenómeno de El Palmar. Este tuvo que darle la vuelta a un 2-4 adverso en la manga inicial y tres pelotas de set (15-40 y ventaja) porque sigue en el proceso para encontrar su mejor servicio. El primer cabeza de serie lucía una nueva equipación de tonos naranjas que le acompañará hasta las ATP Finals de Turín. El campeón de siete grandes le puso todas las ganas que hay que ponerle para firmar otra remontada marca de la casa. Tuvo que esperar a la muerte súbita para tomar la delantera en el marcador. En la continuación, volvió a levantar un 0-2 adverso con la facilidad de los elegidos. Suyos fueron los siguientes cuatro juegos. Michelsen volvió a escena apoyado en el cuarto y quinto saque perdido de su adversario. Alex llegó a sacar para firmar las tablas, con 5-4, y dispuso de dos pelotas de set, que se sumaban a las tres de la manga anterior. A la sexta fue la vencida para él. Con una frescura mental, impropia a estas alturas de temporada, Alcaraz ve huecos donde no los hay. Sólo así se entiende el 6-1 de traca final. El servicio es, ahora mismo, el aspecto a mejorar. En los octavos del sábado, con un día de descanso de por medio, se las verá con el italiano Matteo Arnaldi, el 37 del ranking y al que derrotó en los dos precedentes entre ambos. La lesión de muñeca está más que olvidada. Desde su regreso a la competición, seis partidos ganado y uno perdido, los cuartos del Abierto de los Estados Unidos con Ben Shelton. Alcaraz salió vivo del 'virus' de la Laver Cup. Y es que la mayoría de los jugadores participantes se han despedido a la primera en Tokio y Pekín. En esa lista de víctimas están Flavio Cobolli, Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud, Brandon Nakashima, Ignacio Buse y Arthur Fery.

articles.title: Horario y dónde ver la segunda ronda de Tokio entre Alcaraz y Arnaldi
articles.standfirst: El murciano ha decantado a su favor los dos precedentes con el italiano
articles.summary: El murciano ha decantado a su favor los dos precedentes con el italiano
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, tras su exitoso debut en el Open 500 de Tokio ante Alex Michelsen, tendrá un día de descanso antes de cruzarse en los octavos con Matteo Arnaldi. El italiano, el 37 del ranking a sus 25 años, tiene como mejor resultado las semifinales de Roland Garros 2026. Alcaraz se impuso en los dos precedentes entre ambos: octavos del US Open 2023 y la segunda ronda de Indian Wells 2024. El italiano dejó en la cuneta en el debut al prometedor tenista local, Rei Sakamoto. El partido de segunda ronda de Tokio entre Alcaraz y Arnaldi se disputará este sábado 3 de octubre en la sesión de tarde de la central del Ariake Coliseum, en un horario todavía por confirmar. El ATP 500 de Tokio se podrá ver en TV a través de Movistar+, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: No tennis medal for India at Asian Games for first time in 40 years
articles.summary: India's tennis campaign at the Asian Games ended without a medal on Thursday, with Sumit Nagal's quarterfinal defeat bringing the curtains down on a
articles.body: India's tennis campaign at the Asian Games ended without a medal on Thursday, with Sumit Nagal's quarterfinal defeat bringing the curtains down on a disappointing outing for the country.Nagal, India's top-ranked singles player, was the last Indian left in the medal race after the doubles pairs were knocked out on Wednesday. But the 29-year-old lost 4-6, 4-6 to China's Yibing Wu in one hour and 38 minutes.It means India will return from the Asian Games without a tennis medal for the first time since 1986.Since 1990, India had won at least one tennis medal at every edition of the continental event. This time, however, the country could not continue that run despite entering the competition with hopes of winning at least three medals.Nagal's exit ends India's hopesNagal had carried India's singles hopes into the quarterfinal after beating Hong in the previous round and then overcoming Fomin. But Wu proved too strong for the Indian, who fought hard but could not convert his chances.India coach Ashutosh Singh said the team wanted better results, especially given the experience in the squad."We obviously would have wanted stronger results, particularly given the quality and experience within the team."Singh admitted that the competition was "extremely high" but felt India's singles players needed to make more of their opportunities."Sumit Nagal competed hard in his matches. First beating Hong for the first time in his career, then overcoming Fomin, he did what was required. Even today, Sumit managed to create multiple opportunities but somehow was unable to convert them."DK (Dhakshineswar) has shown his playing level on the Tour but needs more work to sustain his short bursts into good performance through a physically demanding multiple week national campaign if he sees himself as being the torch bearer of the team," Singh said.Doubles pairs also fall shortIndia had hoped that its doubles players would keep the country's medal tradition alive after Nagal's exit.However, Yuki Bhambri and N Sriram Balaji also failed to reach the podium.Balaji and Anirudh Chandrasekar, as well as Bhambri and Dhakshineswar Suresh, lost in the quarterfinals. Dhakshineswar had also exited in the third round of the men's singles. The women's doubles and mixed doubles combinations also could not convert their opportunities into medals.Talking about the doubles, Singh said, Bhambri and Bhosale got a tough Taipei team."The doubles combinations were finalised based on the overall team requirements and the performances and circumstances leading into the event. Unfortunately, we could not convert that opportunity into medals."Yuki and Rutuja were beaten by the Grand Slam champion Hseih who brought all her high level experience and her partner too was playing very attacking tennis."Singh added," As a team, we take responsibility for the results. There is no point in looking for excuses. At the same time, a proper assessment has to consider the conditions, scheduling, preparation and the quality of opposition rather than looking only at the final scorelines."India had a strong medal traditionIndia's last singles medals at the Asian Games came in 2018, when Prajnesh Gunneswaran and Ankita Raina won bronze medals in Jakarta. The country also had a major doubles presence through Rohan Bopanna, who rose to the world No. 1 ranking and helped India win gold medals at the Asian Games.After Bopanna's retirement, the responsibility was expected to be carried by players such as Bhambri and Balaji. But neither could make it to the podium in Japan.India also missed out on singles medals at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games, where Nagal lost in the quarterfinals and Ramkumar Ramanathan went out in the third round.Focus turns to the next generationNagal is already 29, which means he will be 33 when the next Asian Games are held in Doha in 2030. The result has once again brought the focus on India's next generation of tennis players and the need to prepare them for the international stage.AITA interim Secretary General Sunder Iyer said the players had given their best but accepted that the federation needs to do more."Players have tried to do their best. We reached three quarter-finals and were close to medals. As an association we need to see how to give more support to our players, juniors and professionals enabling them to do better," Iyer told PTI.Coach praises team spiritDespite the disappointing results, Singh said the players remained together throughout the campaign. The coach signed off by acknowledging "the way the players stayed together as a group.""There were difficult moments, selections and combinations that naturally bring pressure but the team maintained professionalism and supported one another throughout the campaign," he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alex Eala loses Asian Games semifinal to China’s Wang Xiyu
articles.summary: World number 18 Eala was beaten 3-6, 6-3, 6-2 by 85th-ranked Xiyu, who will face compatriot Zhang Shuai in the final.
articles.body:
Alex Eala’s hopes of a maiden Asian Games gold medal and qualification for ⁠⁠the 2028 Los ⁠⁠Angeles Olympics tennis tournament have been crushed by China’s unheralded Wang Xiyu in the semifinals.

World number 85 Xiyu rallied to a 3-6 6-3 6-2 win over the Filipino top ⁠⁠seed at the games on Thursday.

Eala, the Southeast Asian nation’s first WTA title winner and a fan favourite on tour, was consigned to her second singles bronze medal and third in total, having ⁠⁠also taken the mixed doubles bronze at Hangzhou three years ago.

The 21-year-old gave up the chance to earn ranking points and prize money at the concurrent China Open to represent the Philippines in Nagoya and may get a fine and ranking penalty from the WTA for skipping ‌‌the mandatory event in Beijing.

“I’m really happy to have experienced this, to experience the support … and to be with the team and, yeah, to compete for the country,” she said after the match.

The world number 18 was on track for her first Asian Games final but her level dropped in the second set before she crumbled to a 4-1 deficit in the third.

The 85th-ranked Wang ⁠⁠fought off break points against the increasingly desperate Eala before ⁠⁠serving out the match to love at Higashiyama Park Tennis Center.

“[Wang] was more consistent. I had a couple of ups and downs during the match, which is something I have to talk to my team ⁠⁠about and process,” said Eala.

Wang will meet 37-year-old Zhang Shuai in an all-China final.

She may have her hands full against former ⁠⁠Wimbledon and Australian Open quarterfinalist Zhang, who rolled back ⁠⁠the years to beat Kazakh Yulia Putintseva 6-4 6-2.

Zhang has medalled at three previous Asian Games, taking silver in the 2018 singles in Jakarta and a team gold at the 2010 Guangzhou Games.

She will ‌‌be in her 40s when the next games launch in Doha in 2030 but was not ruling out playing.

“I always feel like this may be my last games. But ‌‌look, ‌‌aren’t I here again?” she said.

“As long as you don’t give up on yourself, no one else in this world can give you that death sentence.”

articles.title: Rafa Jódar es la séptima víctima de la Laver Cup y encadena dos primeras rondas
articles.standfirst: El madrileño, cuarto cabeza de serie en Tokio, cede a manos del 'qualy' Vallejo
articles.summary: El madrileño, cuarto cabeza de serie en Tokio, cede a manos del 'qualy' Vallejo
articles.body: La cercanía de la Laver Cup con los torneos 500 de Pekín y Tokio ha convertido las primeras rondas en una escabechina de favoritos. Hasta siete tenistas presentes el fin de semana en el O2 Arena de Londres se han despedido en su debut en la gira asiática. A Taylor Fritz, Flavio Cobolli, Casper Ruud, Brandon Nakashima, Ignacio Buse y Arthur Fery se le has unido Rafa Jódar. El madrileño, cuarto cabeza de serie en el Open 500 de Tokio, se ha despedido en el estreno ante el 'qualy', Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, el 56 de las listas ATP, por 6-1 y 6-3. Jódar, en su primera campaña como profesional, encadena por primera vez dos derrotas en la primera ronda de un torneo del circuito. Cabe recordar que cayó en el debut del US Open con el chino Bu. A Rafa no le respondió el servicio, un aspecto fundamental en superficie rápida. Hasta seis veces lo perdió ante un eléctrico Vallejo, que venía rodado y con la confianza de haber superado la fase previa. El joven del Club de Tenis Chamartín, con opciones matemáticas de alcanzar el 'top10' en esta gira asiática, se queda a 491 puntos de Alex de Miñaur, que cierra las posiciones de privilegio. El calendario de Jódar le conducirá ahora al Masters 1000 de Shanghái, Basilea y el TMS de París como cierre del curso a la espera de la convocatoria de David Ferrer para las finales de la Copa Davis de Bolonia.

articles.title: Davidovich paga el cansancio de Chengdu y cede ante Berrettini en Tokio
articles.standfirst: El malagueño, campeón el martes, pierde dos días después sin margen de recuperación
articles.summary: El malagueño, campeón el martes, pierde dos días después sin margen de recuperación
articles.body: El tenis masculino español ha pasado de poder asegurar la presencia de un representante en los cuartos de Tokio (salía del duelo fratricida entre Rafa Jódar y Alejandro Davidovich) a quedarse sin ninguno. Alejandro Davidovich, el 26 del ranking ATP, pagó el cansancio. Campeón el martes en Chengdu, no pudo acceder 48 horas después a la segunda ronda de Tokio. La culpa la tuvo Matteo Berrettini, su verdugo por 1-6 y 7-6 y 6-4. Mientras a Davidovich le dio el físico fue mejor que su rival italiano. La derrota en el segundo parcial significó un antes y un después en el partido. Berrettini empezó la manga de desempate con una renta de 3-0, que ya no dejó escapar. "Yo siempre estoy para la Copa Davis, otra cosa es que me llamen", decía tras levantar su segundo título como profesional en Chengdu. Álex está terminando el año con la misma fuerza que el anterior, donde alcanzó la final de Basilea y los octavos del Masters 1000 de París.
